translationRepairs: Hu Ying said, "Emperor Taizu laid the imperial tombs here to show his line a capital they must not abandon."
Hu Ying said, "Emperor Wen laid the imperial tombs here to show his line a capital they must not abandon."
s0075 has 文皇, Emperor Wen (Yongle/Chengzu), not Taizu (太祖); the proposed Emperor Wen matches the Chinese while preserving the rest of the idiomatic sentence.
The great ministers asked the empress dowager to install the prince as heir apparent and have the Prince of Fu act as regent.
The great ministers asked the empress dowager to install the prince as heir apparent and have the Prince of Cheng act as regent.
s0152 has 郕王, the Prince of Cheng; Fu (福) is unsupported, and Prince of Cheng restores the correct princely title.
The great ministers together asked the Empress Dowager to establish the prince as heir apparent and order the Prince of Fu to govern as regent.
The great ministers together asked the Empress Dowager to establish the prince as heir apparent and order the Prince of Cheng to govern as regent.
The same focus unit 命郕王攝政 names the Prince of Cheng; the literal’s Prince of Fu is the same title error and the proposed Cheng fix is accurate.
The next year he came to court and was kept at the Nanjing ministry of rites, soon advanced to minister.
The next year he came to court and was kept at the traveling-court Ministry of Rites, soon advanced to minister.
s0054 has 行在禮部, the traveling-court Ministry of Rites; Nanjing (南京) is not in the Chinese, and the proposed replacement corrects that misidentification.
Then Huang Ying, native-office prefect of Siming, memorialized asking for it.
Then Huang Zeng, native-office prefect of Siming, memorialized asking for it.
s0214 names 黃矰, read Huang Zeng; Ying invents a reading of 矰, and Huang Zeng restores the correct personal name.
Between Yingzong and Jingtai the realm was in upheaval and minds were unsettled; many who held power flattered to please.
Between Yingzong and Jingtai, when the realm's situation had just changed and people watched and waited, many ministers who held power and handled affairs flattered to please.

國勢初更 is a newly changed political situation, not upheaval, and 人心觀望 is wait-and-see watching, not unsettled minds; 執政任事之臣 also includes those handling affairs. The proposal rightly rejects the overstated before reading, but 'national situation was newly changed' and 'people's hearts were watchful' are stiff calques.
